rationale: The plan correctly recognizes that STAR/featureCounts integers are gene-level and enter DESeq2 via DESeqDataSetFromMatrix with no tximport and no length offset, and it says so explicitly; the edgeR QL cross-check is framed as robustness only, with the primary inference fixed in advance. QC (library sizes, blind VST, PCA on top-500 variable genes, distance heatmap) precedes the fit with an explicit no-drop policy, the filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size) is minimal and justified, normalization is internal (median-of-ratios / TMM) with an explicit ban on pre-scaling, and the design ~condition with control set as reference level and the contrast written out is fully specified. FDR is BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, apeglm shrinkage for reporting, lfcThreshold rather than a post hoc fold-change cut, plus p-value histogram and NA-padj accounting by cause. The report step is exemplary: versions, design, thresholds, tested and significant counts, plots, and an n=3 power statement placed before the gene tables. Enrichment is the only weak point: the question asks only which genes differ, so GSEA is scope creep rather than warranted, though it is at least well specified (Wald-statistic ranking, tested-gene universe, 15-500 size window, named collection with version, seed, leading edges, no ORA on a short list).
